name: scriptura-backend
description: Scriptura — Divinetalk internal AI blog automation tool (API)

scripts.db:reset: sequelize-cli db:seed:undo:all && sequelize-cli db:migrate:undo:all && sequelize-cli db:migrate && sequelize-cli db:seed:all

//dependencies: sqlite3 is a devDependency, NOT a production one. Production runs MySQL; sqlite3 is
used only by the Jest suite and by dev:demo, and Sequelize requires a dialect's
driver lazily, so the production build never loads it.
This matters for the Docker image: sqlite3 has an install script that downloads a
prebuilt binary over the network, which made `npm ci --omit=dev` fail in the
container with npm's 'Exit handler never called!' — a crash, not a clear error.
Keeping it out of the production tree removes that network fetch entirely and
shrinks the image. Do not promote it back to dependencies.
//scripts: dev      — the real thing: MySQL, live AI providers if keys are set. Needs a database.
dev:demo — no database required. Boots the same Express app on in-memory SQLite with
the demo seed and the deterministic mock AI providers, on port 5000 so the
frontend's CRA proxy finds it. Data resets on every restart, and generated
content is canned. Use it to look at the UI; never as a deployment path.
//overrides: htmlparser2: sanitize-html pulls v12, which is pure ESM with no CommonJS build.
Node 24 can require() ESM so the app itself runs fine, but Jest's CommonJS runtime
cannot load it, which breaks every test that touches sanitisation. v9 is the last
CommonJS major and exposes the identical Parser API sanitize-html uses.
Remove this override once the suite moves to Jest's native ESM mode.
